# Dataset – AI-Based Electrical Load Classification

**Synthetic**, generated by a physics-based simulator (`src/simulator.py`), 21 balanced classes
(3 behaviours x 7 compositions). Regenerate / resize: `python scripts/generate_dataset.py --n-train 500`.

## features/  (what the XGBoost heads train on)
| file | rows | SNR (dB) | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| train.csv | 4200 (200/class) | 10-55 | training (noise-augmented) |
| calibration.csv | 1050 | 10-55 | temperature scaling + conformal |
| test_noisy.csv | 1260 | 15-50 | main test |
| test_clean.csv | 1260 | 40-60 | clean test |

Columns: `behavior` (CC/CP/CZ), `composition` (R/L/C/RL/RC/LC/RLC), then 75 features:
static (v_rms_*, i_rms_*, p_*, q_*, pf_*, z_*, phi_end, thd_v/i, ratio_v/i/p), dynamic P-V/I-V exponents (n_i, n_s, n_p, n_q, n_phi, n_g, n_b ...),
harmonic admittance (ih2-9, g_h, b_h, yr_h, dphi_h, vh_h, yslope, phase_slope), transient (tr_*),
waveform (liss_*, cf_*, snr_*_db, f_est). Empty cells = NaN (e.g. n_p undefined for purely reactive loads; XGBoost handles NaN natively).

## raw/  (voltage & current waveforms)
* `waveforms.npz`: `voltage`, `current` (630 x 1536, float32, 12 cycles @ 6400 Hz), `fs`, `behavior`, `composition`
* `metadata.csv`: per-record labels + simulation parameters (frequency `f`, sag/swell `dv`, `snr`, topology, harmonic scale, R/L/C, parasitics rl/rc)
* `sample_records/<BEH>_<COMP>.csv`: 21 single records (`time_s,voltage,current`) – usable with
  `python deploy/predict_cli.py dataset/raw/sample_records/CP_RLC.csv` (rename columns not needed) or POST to `/predict`.

## Physics of the labels
Behaviour: i = i_lin / env^k, k = 0 (CZ), 1 (CC), 2 (CP), env = supply sag/swell (8-25 %).
Composition: random series/parallel R/L/C networks with winding resistance and capacitor ESR; switching transient at random angle.

## Using your own measured data
Provide `voltage`, `current` columns sampled at >= 1536 samples (>= 12 cycles, any fs; resampled to 6.4 kHz),
ideally with a supply-voltage step/sag/swell inside the record (needed for CC/CP/CZ). Label and run
`extract_features(v, i)` from `src/features.py` to create rows in the same format.

## Exploratory analysis
Run `python analyze_datasets.py` or execute the analysis cell in `data.ipynb` to profile all four feature
tables. The `analysis_output/` directory contains the full column and missingness report, categorical
distributions, numeric feature statistics, feature and label correlations, and CSVs for label cross-tabs.
All generated PNG visualizations are saved in `analysis_output/plots/`.
